name: thirty_one_raids
caption: why do raiders always follow grandpa home 😶
logline: A boy's grandpa has saved their village from thirty-one raids, and every one started the night he came home; when Grandpa is too tired to fight, the boy drinks his medicine to be brave like him.
question: why tf do raiders show up every time grandpa comes home?
premise: The villagers throw bread at Grandpa when he walks by: he has saved them from 31 raids, and keeps a totem from each on his wall. Every raid started the night he came home. He says the raiders follow him because he beats them. He hunts at the old pillager tower and brings back grey bottles he calls his medicine; he drinks one at the village gate and tells the boy to lock the door. Since Grandma died, a raid is the only time anyone is glad to see him.
twist: The medicine is an ominous bottle: drinking it gives Bad Omen, and walking into a village with it starts a raid. Grandpa has been bringing every raid himself, so the village will need him. Tonight he's too tired to fight, so the boy drinks it to be brave; the raid horn sounds, and Grandpa tells him: now they'll love you too.

N.name: me
N.profile: a boy of about eleven who worships his grandpa, telling the story low and steady; the pride drains out of him as he goes
N.on_screen: pov (never seen); hotbar: empty hand, then the ominous bottle (S12)

Grandpa.name: Grandpa
Grandpa.profile: an old fighter, gravelly and dry, proud and very tired; few words, never wasted; calls the boy 'kid'
Grandpa.on_screen: a player with an old man's skin (grey beard, brown coat), a crossbow on his back; on screen from S01

requests.direction: A village at dusk after many raids. A boy tells how his grandpa saves the village; the grandpa speaks rarely, gravelly and tired.

sfx.note: villagers cheering as they throw him bread
the raid horn, far, on the hill: the reveal

lines.text: Grandpa has saved / our village / from THIRTY-ONE / RAIDS.
lines.say: Grandpa has saved our village <short pause> from thirty-one raids.
lines.direction: proud, hushed; a held beat before the number

lines.text: Every single one / started the night / he came HOME.
lines.direction: the pride draining; slower; it lands on the last word
repeating what he was told, believing it

lines.text: They know / who BEATS them, / kid.
lines.direction: dry and proud, not looking up from his work

lines.text: He keeps a TOTEM / from every raid. / Thirty-one / on his WALL.
Since Grandma died, / it's the only time / anyone's GLAD / to see him.
lines.say: Since Grandma died, <short pause> it's the only time anyone's glad to see him.
lines.direction: softer, a sadness he only half understands

lines.text: He hunts / at the old TOWER / on the hill.
lines.direction: a little in awe of the place

lines.text: He brings back / grey BOTTLES. / He's got / a whole CHEST.
He calls it / his MEDICINE. / He drinks it / at the GATE.
lines.direction: steady; a tiny hitch before the last part

lines.text: Lock the DOOR, / kid. / They're COMING.
lines.say: Lock the door, kid. <short pause> They're coming.
lines.direction: calm, certain, almost bored; he knows exactly when

lines.text: Tonight / he was too TIRED / to fight.
So I drank / his MEDICINE. / I wanted / to be BRAVE / like HIM.
lines.say: So I drank his medicine. <short pause> I wanted to be brave like him.
lines.direction: a small brave breath first; the last words proud and young
lines.hold_note: no words: the horn on the hill, banners and torches rising over the ridge (S13)

lines.text: Now they'll / love YOU / too, kid.
lines.say: Now they'll love you too, kid.
lines.direction: gentle, tired, almost proud: the warmth is the worst part; a breath before the last word
